<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt 1.0in;text-indent:-1.0in;"><a name="Item7aQuantitativeAndQualitativeD_232957"></a><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">ITEM 7A</font><font size="1" style="font-size:8.5pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>QUANTITATIVE AND QUALITATIVE DISCLOSURES
ABOUT MARKET RISK</p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 1.0in;text-indent:-1.0in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
primary objective of our investment activities, other than activities relating
to ENS and potential acquisitions, is to preserve principal and maintain
liquidity, while at the same time maximizing the yield we receive from our
investment portfolio.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Changes
in prevailing interest rates will cause the yield on our investments.&#160; To minimize this risk, we maintain our
portfolio of cash equivalents, short-term investments and marketable securities
in commercial paper, non-government debt securities, money market funds, highly
liquid U.S. Treasury notes and federal agency notes and other low risk
investments.&#160; We view these high grade
securities within our portfolio as having similar market risk characteristics.
The weighted-average interest rate of the portfolio was 3.4% at October&nbsp;31,
2005.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Currently
almost all our revenues and expenses are denominated in U.S. dollars and, as a
result, we have experienced no significant foreign exchange gains and losses to
date.&#160; We conduct only limited
transactions in foreign currencies, and we do not anticipate that foreign
exchange gains or losses will be significant in the foreseeable future.&#160; We have not engaged in foreign currency
hedging activities to date.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt 1.0in;text-indent:-1.0in;"><a name="Item8_ConsolidatedFinancialStatem_233003"></a><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">ITEM 8.</font><font size="1" style="font-size:8.5pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Information with respect to this item is contained
in the financial statements appearing in Item 15 of this report.&#160; Such information is incorporated by
reference.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><a name="ReportOfIndependentRegisteredPubl_001914"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Report of Independent Registered Public Accounting

<p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:normal;">&nbsp;</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">To the Board of Directors
and Stockholders <br>
NWH,&nbsp;Inc.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">New York, New York</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We have audited the
consolidated balance sheet of NWH,&nbsp;Inc. and subsidiaries as of October&nbsp;31,
2005, and the related consolidated statements of income, comprehensive income,
stockholders&#146; equity and cash flows for the year then ended. These financial
statements are the responsibility of the Company&#146;s management. Our
responsibility is to express an opinion on these financial statements based on
our audit.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We conducted our audit in
accordance with the standards of the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board
(United States).&#160; Those standards require
that we plan and perform the audit to obtain reasonable assurance about whether
the financial statements are free of material misstatement.&#160; An audit includes examining, on a test basis,
evidence supporting the amounts and disclosures in the financial
statements.&#160; An audit also includes
assessing the accounting principles used and significant estimates made by
management, as well as evaluating the overall financial statement presentation.&#160; We believe that our audit provides a
reasonable basis for our opinion.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In our opinion, the
consolidated financial statements referred to above present fairly, in all
material respects, the financial position of NWH,&nbsp;Inc. and subsidiaries as
of October&nbsp;31, 2005, and the results of their operations and their cash
flows for the year then ended in conformity with U.S. generally accepted
accounting principles.</font></p>

<div>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:black;font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;page-break-after:auto;text-indent:-.4in;"><a name="a1_CompanyOperations_002149"></a><b><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">1.</font></b><font size="1" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:8.5pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">Company Operations</font></p>

<p style="color:black;font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;page-break-after:auto;text-indent:-.4in;"><b><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:normal;">&nbsp;</font></b></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">NWH,&nbsp;Inc. (the &#147;Company&#148;), a Delaware corporation
organized on August&nbsp;31, 1993, is an electronic commerce and communications
company.&#160; The Company currently owns
substantially all of the common stock of Electronic Network Systems Inc., (&#147;ENS&#148;),
a payer services organization that connects healthcare payers and providers
using state of the art proprietary software and telecommunications services for
most healthcare payment and insurance validation transactions.&#160; In addition to this business, the Company
continues to pursue acquisitions of interests in healthcare and other
strategically linked areas.&#160; The Company
may acquire or invest in other businesses.</font></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:black;font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;page-break-after:auto;text-indent:-.4in;"><b><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">2.</font></b><font size="1" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:8.5pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">Summary of Significant Accounting Policies</font></p>

<p style="color:black;font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;page-break-after:auto;text-indent:-.4in;"><b><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:normal;">&nbsp;</font></b></p>

<p style="color:black;font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;page-break-after:auto;"><b><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">Basis of Consolidation</font></b></p>

<p style="color:black;font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;page-break-after:auto;"><b><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:normal;">&nbsp;</font></b></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">The consolidated financial statements include the accounts of
the Company and its majority-owned subsidiaries.&#160; All significant intercompany transactions and
balances have been eliminated in consolidation.&#160;
ENS&#146; fiscal year end is September&nbsp;30, and, as such, elimination of
intercompany transactions were made accordingly. (See Note 12.)</font></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:black;font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;page-break-after:auto;"><b><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">Cash and Cash Equivalents</font></b></p>

<p style="color:black;font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;page-break-after:auto;"><b><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:normal;">&nbsp;</font></b></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">Cash and cash equivalents include all highly liquid
investments with original maturities of three months or less and are readily
convertible to cash.&#160; The Company
routinely invests all surplus operating funds in various money market
funds.&#160; These funds generally invest in
highly liquid U.S. government and agency obligations.</font></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:black;font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;page-break-after:auto;"><b><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">Marketable Securities</font></b></p>

<p style="color:black;font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;page-break-after:auto;"><b><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:normal;">&nbsp;</font></b></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">Marketable securities at October&nbsp;31, 2004 consist of
investments in United States treasury bills. The U.S. treasury bills are
classified as held to maturity and are valued at amortized cost, which is
adjusted for amortization from the date of purchase to maturity.&#160; The Company liquidated its investment in Bell
South common stock in September&nbsp;2004.&#160;
Investment income or loss including realized gains and losses on
investments, interest and dividends is included in the statement of
income.&#160; Unrealized gains and losses for
the Bell South common stock are recorded, net of tax, as a separate component
of stockholders&#146; equity.&#160; Gains and
losses on securities sold are determined based on the specific identification
method.</font></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">The Company utilized written call options to protect its
position in BellSouth common stock, preserve its tax basis and reduce equity
price risk. Under the provisions of Statement of Financial Accounting Standards
(&#147;SFAS&#148;) No.&nbsp;133, Accounting for Derivative Instruments and Hedging
Activities, written call options are measured at fair value on the balance
sheet with unrealized gains and losses recognized in the statement of income.</font></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:black;font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;page-break-after:auto;"><b><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">Trade and Other Receivables</font></b></p>

<p style="color:black;font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;page-break-after:auto;"><b><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:normal;">&nbsp;</font></b></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">Trade accounts receivable are recorded at their invoiced
amount.&#160; The Company maintains an
allowance for doubtful accounts for estimated losses resulting from the
inability of its customers to make payments when due or within a reasonable
period of time thereafter.&#160; Estimates are
based on experience, current trends, credit policy and a percentage of accounts
receivable by aging category.&#160; If the
financial condition of the Company&#146;s customers were to deteriorate, resulting
in an impairment of their ability to make required payments, additional
allowances may be required.&#160; The Company
does not have any off-balance sheet credit exposure.</font></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">When assets are retired or disposed of, the loss and
accumulated depreciation and amortization are eliminated and the resulting
profit or loss is recognized in the statement of income.</font></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:black;font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;page-break-after:auto;"><b><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">Internally Developed Software</font></b></p>

<p style="color:black;font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;page-break-after:auto;"><b><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:normal;">&nbsp;</font></b></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">The Company capitalizes purchased software which is ready for
service and development costs for software incurred from the time the preliminary
project stage is completed until the software is ready for use.&#160; Under the provisions of Statement of Position
98-1, &#147;Accounting for the Costs of Computer Software Developed or Obtained for
Internal Use&#148; (SOP 98-1), the Company capitalizes costs associated with
software developed or obtained for internal use when both the preliminary
project state is completed and the Company management has authorized further
funding for the project which it deems probable to be completed and used to
perform the function intended.&#160;
Capitalized costs include only (1)&nbsp;external direct costs of
materials and services consumed in developing or obtaining internal-use
software, (2)&nbsp;payroll and payroll-related costs for employees who are
directly associated with and who devote time to the internal-use software
project, and (3)&nbsp;interest costs incurred, when material, while developing
internal-use software.&#160; Capitalization of
such costs ceases no later than the point at which the project is substantially
complete and ready for its intended purpose.</font></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">Research and development costs and computer software
maintenance costs related to software development are expensed as
incurred.&#160; Capitalized software
development costs are amortized using the straight-line method generally over
four years, not to exceed the expected life of the product or related
contract.&#160; The carrying value of
capitalized software development costs is regularly reviewed by the Company,
and a loss is recognized if the value of estimated undiscounted cash flows
related to the asset falls below the unamortized costs. Amortization expense
was $1,374,013, $1,083,675 and $612,246 for the years ended October&nbsp;31,
2005, 2004 and 2003, respectively.</font></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:black;font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;page-break-after:auto;"><b><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">Impairment of Long-Lived Assets</font></b></p>

<p style="color:black;font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;page-break-after:auto;"><b><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:normal;">&nbsp;</font></b></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">The Company investigates potential impairments of its
long-lived assets when evidence exists that events or changes in circumstances
may have made recovery of an asset&#146;s carrying value unlikely.&#160; An impairment loss is recognized when the sum
of the expected undiscounted future net cash flows is less than the carrying
amount of the asset.</font></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">The Company applies the provisions of SFAS No.&nbsp;144 (FAS
144), &#147;Accounting for the Impairment or Disposal of Long Lived Assets&#148;.&#160; This statement provides guidance on the
recognition of impairment losses on long-lived assets to be held and used or to
be disposed of and also broadens the definition of what constitutes a
discounted operation and how the results of a discontinued operation are to be
measured and presented.&#160; Recoverability
of assets to be held and used is measured by a comparison of the carrying
amount of an asset to future new cash flows expected to</font></p>

<p style="color:black;font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;page-break-after:auto;"><b><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">Goodwill</font></b></p>

<p style="color:black;font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;page-break-after:auto;"><b><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:normal;">&nbsp;</font></b></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">Goodwill represents the excess of the purchase price over the
net assets of acquired companies.&#160; Under
the provisions of SFAS No.&nbsp;141, &#147;Business Combinations&#148; and SFAS No.&nbsp;142,
&#147;Goodwill and Other Intangible Assets&#148; goodwill and intangible assets that have
an indefinite life are not amortized, but are subject to at least an annual
impairment test.&#160; Other intangible assets
that have finite useful lives are amortized over their useful life.</font></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">As required by SFAS No.&nbsp;142, the Company assessed the

not record an impairment charge as a result.</font></p>

<p style="color:black;font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;page-break-after:auto;"><b><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">Concentration of Credit Risk</font></b></p>

<p style="color:black;font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;page-break-after:auto;"><b><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:normal;">&nbsp;</font></b></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">Financial instruments which potentially subject the Company

collateral for accounts receivable.&#160; Cash
is placed into financial institutions with high credit ratings.&#160; Concentration of risks in receivables with
respect to providers and payers other than the major customer mentioned in
Revenue Recognition below is mitigated based on the number of customers and
ongoing credit evaluations of existing customers.&#160; The Company has deposits on hand that exceed
the limits of the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation.</font></p>

<p style="color:black;font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;page-break-after:auto;"><b><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">Fair Value of Financial Instruments</font></b></p>

<p style="color:black;font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;page-break-after:auto;"><b><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:normal;">&nbsp;</font></b></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">Cash equivalents comprise money market funds whose carrying
amounts approximate fair value due to the short-term maturity of the
instruments.</font></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">Long-term debt relates principally to equipment lease
obligations and a note payable to a former related party.&#160; Interest rates on the debt approximate the
rates available at October&nbsp;31, 2005 and 2004 and the Company believes that
the carrying value of debt at October&nbsp;31, 2005 approximates fair value.</font></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:black;font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;page-break-after:auto;"><b><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">Revenue Recognition</font></b></p>

<p style="color:black;font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;page-break-after:auto;"><b><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:normal;">&nbsp;</font></b></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">Service revenue and revenue associated with electronic
transactions to and from providers and payers is recognized as earned in the
period the services are provided.&#160;
Installation revenue and the related costs are deferred when received or
incurred and recognized over a twelve month period corresponding with the term
of the service contract.&#160; Development
fees and the related costs are deferred when received or incurred and
recognized over the period corresponding with the term of the related contract
(one to seven years).</font></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 28.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During
fiscal years 2005, 2004 and 2003, the Company had one customer that made up
37%, 42% and 39% of total revenues and 37%, 49% and 42% of net accounts
receivable, as of October&nbsp;31, 2005, 2004 and 2003, respectively. (See Note
12)</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 28.5pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Cost of
Services</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 28.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Cost
of services are expensed as incurred and consist primarily of labor, related
overhead costs of employees and depreciation and amortization of equipment and
capitalized software directly involved in or related to activities which
generate or are anticipated to generate revenues.&#160; Included in direct cost of revenue is depreciation
of furniture and</font></p>

<div>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">equipment
and amortization of capitalized software costs of $1,478,134, $1,276,141 and
$926,370 for the years ended October&nbsp;31, 2005, 2004 and 2003,
respectively.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 28.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 28.5pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Advertising</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 28.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 28.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Advertising
and promotion costs are expensed as incurred.&#160;
Advertising and promotion expense was $79,142, $55,951 and $70,238 for
the years ended October&nbsp;31, 2005, 2004 and 2003, respectively.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 28.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:black;font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;page-break-after:auto;"><b><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">Income Taxes</font></b></p>

<p style="color:black;font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;page-break-after:auto;"><b><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:normal;">&nbsp;</font></b></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">Deferred tax assets and liabilities are recognized for the
expected future tax consequences of events that have been included in the
financial statements or tax returns.&#160;
Under this method, deferred tax assets and liabilities are determined
based on the difference between the financial reporting and tax bases of assets
and liabilities using enacted tax rates in effect for the year in which the
differences are expected to reverse.&#160;
Valuation allowances are established when necessary to reduce deferred
tax assets to the amounts expected to be realized.</font></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:black;font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;page-break-after:auto;"><b><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">Stock-Based Compensation</font></b></p>

<p style="color:black;font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;page-break-after:auto;"><b><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:normal;">&nbsp;</font></b></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">At October&nbsp;31, 2005, the Company has stock-based
compensation plans, which are described more fully in Note 14.&#160; The Company adopted the disclosure-only
provisions of SFAS No.&nbsp;148, &#147;Accounting for Stock-Based Compensation
Transition and Disclosure, an amendment of FAS&nbsp;123.&#148;&#160; This statement encourages, but does not
require, companies to adopt a fair value based method for determining expenses
related to stock-based compensation. The Company continues to account for
stock-based compensation using the intrinsic value method as prescribed under
Accounting Principles Board Opinion No.&nbsp;25, &#147;Accounting for Stock Issued
to Employees,&#148; and related Interpretations. Accordingly, no compensation cost
has been recognized with regard to options granted under the Plan in the
accompanying financial statements.</font></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">The following table illustrates the pro forma effect on net
income and net income per common share if the Company had applied the fair
value recognition provisions of FAS 123 to stock-based employee compensation.</font></p>

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">


<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">These pro forma adjustments to net income and net income per
common share assume fair values of each option grant estimated using the
Black-Scholes option pricing formula.&#160;
The more significant assumptions underlying the determination of such
fair value for options granted in 2005, 2004 and 2003 include:&#160; (i)&nbsp;weighted average risk-free interest
rates of 4.3% in 2005 and 2.93% in 2004 and 2003; (ii)&nbsp;weighted average
expected option life of 5 years; (iii)&nbsp;an expected volatility of 19% in
2005 and 45% in 2004 and 2003; and (iv)&nbsp;an expected dividend yield of 14%
in 2005, 11.5% in 2004 and 0% in 2003.&#160;
The per share weighted average fair value at the dates of grant for
options awarded for the year ended October&nbsp;31, 2005 was $0.27 and the
weighted average exercise price was $14.66.</font></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:black;font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;page-break-after:auto;"><b><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">Net Income Per Common Share</font></b></p>

<p style="color:black;font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;page-break-after:auto;"><b><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:normal;">&nbsp;</font></b></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">Basic earnings per share is computed by dividing net income
by the weighted average number of common shares outstanding during the
period.&#160; Diluted earnings per share is
computed by dividing net income by the sum of the weighted average number of
common shares outstanding plus the dilutive potential common shares.</font></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:black;font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;page-break-after:auto;"><b><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">Use of Estimates</font></b></p>

<p style="color:black;font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;page-break-after:auto;"><b><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:normal;">&nbsp;</font></b></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">The presentation of financial statements in conformity with
accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America requires
the Company&#146;s management to make estimates and assumptions that affect the
reported amounts of assets and liabilities and disclosure of contingent assets
and liabilities at the date of the financial statements, and the reported
amounts of revenues and expenses during the reporting period.&#160; Actual results could differ from those
estimates.</font></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:black;font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;page-break-after:auto;"><b><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">Recently Issued Accounting Pronouncements</font></b></p>

<p style="color:black;font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;page-break-after:auto;"><b><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:normal;">&nbsp;</font></b></p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt 28.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><font style="font-size:10.0pt;">In May&nbsp;2005, the </font>Financial Accounting
Standards Board (FASB)</font> issued
SFAS No.&nbsp;154, &#147;Accounting for Changes and Error Corrections&#148; (FAS 154),
which replaces APB Opinion No.&nbsp;20 &#147;Accounting Changes&#148;, and SFAS No.&nbsp;3,
&#147;Reporting Accounting Changes in Interim Financial Statements&#148;, and changes the
requirements for the accounting for and reporting of a change in accounting
principle. Opinion No.&nbsp;20 previously required that most voluntary changes
in accounting principle be recognized by including in net income of the period
of the change the cumulative effect of changing to the new accounting
principle. FAS 154 requires that the new accounting principle be applied to the
balances of assets and liabilities as of the beginning of the earliest period
for which retrospective application is practicable and that a corresponding
adjustment be made to the opening balance of retained earnings for that period
rather than being reported in the income statement.&#160; The adoption of FAS 154 is not expected to
have a material impact on the Company&#146;s financial position or results of
operations.</p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 28.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 28.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In December&nbsp;2004,
the Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB) issued FASB statement No.&nbsp;123R,
&#147;Share-Based Payment&#148; (FAS 123R), a revision of FASB statement No.&nbsp;123,
&#147;Accounting for Stock-Based Compensation&#148;, which addresses financial accounting
and reporting for costs associated with stock-based compensation.&#160; FAS 123R addresses all forms of share-based
payment (&#147;SBP&#148;) awards, including shares issued under employee stock purchase
plans, stock options, restricted stock and stock appreciation rights.&#160; In accordance with FAS 123R the Company will adopt
the new accounting provisions in the first quarter of 2006.&#160; In March&nbsp;2005, the Staff of the
Securities and Exchange Commission (&#147;SEC&#148;) issued Staff Accounting Bulletin No.&nbsp;107
(&#147;SAB 107&#148;) which provides guidance in the implementation of FAS 123R.&#160; The adoption of FAS&nbsp;123R and SAB 107 are
not expected to have an impact on the Company&#146;s financial position and results
of operations.</font></p>

<p style="color:black;font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;page-break-after:auto;"><b><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></b></p>

<p style="color:black;font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;page-break-after:auto;"><b><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">Reclassifications</font></b></p>

<p style="color:black;font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;page-break-after:auto;"><b><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:normal;">&nbsp;</font></b></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">Certain prior year amounts have been reclassified to conform
to current year presentation, with no effect on consolidated earnings.</font></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:black;font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;page-break-after:auto;text-indent:-.4in;"><b><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">3.</font></b><font size="1" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:8.5pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">ENS</font></p>

<p style="color:black;font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;page-break-after:auto;text-indent:-.4in;"><b><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:normal;">&nbsp;</font></b></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">Between 1996 and 2002, the Company acquired 94% of the
outstanding common stock (assuming conversion of its preferred stock), and with
additional voting rights, 99% control of ENS for an aggregate investment of
$6,854,390.&#160; The acquisitions have been
accounted for under the purchase method of accounting and the results of
operations from the date of purchase have been reflected in</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">the consolidated statement of operations.&#160; The purchase price in excess of the fair

goodwill.</font></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">In January&nbsp;2003, the Company adopted an incentive bonus

providing for payment of approximately 5% of any gain to the Company in the
event of a sale of ENS or a public offering by ENS.</font></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:black;font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;page-break-after:auto;text-indent:-.4in;"><b><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">4.</font></b><font size="1" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:8.5pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">Marketable Securities</font></p>

<p style="color:black;font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;page-break-after:auto;text-indent:-.4in;"><b><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:normal;">&nbsp;</font></b></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">Marketable securities consist of United States treasury bills
as of October&nbsp;31, 2004.</font></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.4in;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:black;font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;page-break-after:auto;text-indent:-.4in;"><b><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">5.</font></b><font size="1" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:8.5pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">Property and Equipment and Internally Developed Software</font></p>

<p style="color:black;font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;page-break-after:auto;text-indent:-.4in;"><b><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:normal;">&nbsp;</font></b></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:black;font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;page-break-after:auto;text-indent:-.4in;"><b><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">6.</font></b><font size="1" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:8.5pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">Long-Term Debt</font></p>

<p style="color:black;font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;page-break-after:auto;text-indent:-.4in;"><b><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:normal;">&nbsp;</font></b></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">The Company&#146;s long-term debt at October&nbsp;31, 2004 is
comprised of capital lease obligations of $11,494 with interest rates ranging
from 10.5% to 8.9%, which was paid in full during fiscal 2005 and a $140,000
subordinated note payable to a former stockholder.&#160; The interest rate for the subordinated note
payable to a former stockholder is the same as that of the ENS Loan Agreement
with the Company.&#160; After the payment of
the borrowings under the ENS Loan Agreement, this note payable and the accrued
interest are due on demand.</font></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">The Company has a $100,000 revolving line of credit agreement
with a bank which expires on April&nbsp;30, 2006.&#160; Borrowings under the line bear interest at
the one month reserve adjusted London Interbank Offered Rate (3.86% at September&nbsp;30,
2005) plus 1.5%.&#160; There were no
borrowings outstanding under this line at October&nbsp;31, 2005.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">As of October&nbsp;31,
2005, there are approximately $1,490,000 of federal net operating loss
carryforwards for tax purposes.&#160; These
net operating losses will expire between 2011 and 2019.&#160; Due to the federal consolidated returns regulations,
the separate Company net operating loss carryforwards of ENS are not
anticipated to be utilized by the group for federal income tax purposes and
therefore a valuation allowance has been recorded.</font></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:black;font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;page-break-after:auto;text-indent:-.4in;"><b><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:normal;">&nbsp;</font></b></p>

payable in cash on February&nbsp;3, 2006, to stockholders of record at the
close of business on January&nbsp;27, 2006.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">The Company
acquired 1,000 and 29,200 shares of its common stock for $14,605 and $369,564
during the years ended October&nbsp;31, 2005 and 2003, respectively, under a
plan that permits the acquisition of up to 20% of the Company&#146;s stock.&#160; No shares were acquired during fiscal 2004.</font></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:black;font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;page-break-after:auto;text-indent:-.4in;"><b><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">11.</font></b><font size="1" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:8.5pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">Sale of Partnership Investment</font></p>

<p style="color:black;font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;page-break-after:auto;text-indent:-.4in;"><b><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:normal;">&nbsp;</font></b></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">During the
year ended October&nbsp;31, 2003, the Company sold its partnership investment
for cash proceeds of $1,421,283 and recognized a gain of $421,253, which is
included in other income.</font></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:black;font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;page-break-after:auto;text-indent:-.4in;"><b><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">12.</font></b><font size="1" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:8.5pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">Arbitration Award</font></p>

<p style="color:black;font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;page-break-after:auto;text-indent:-.4in;"><b><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:normal;">&nbsp;</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company&#146;s arbitration
with a major customer over additional business opportunities was resolved with
an award of $1,000,757 to ENS, which was paid in August, 2005 and has been
shown net of expenses of $441,670 incurred in relation to the proceedings.&#160; Subsequent to ENS&#146; fiscal year end, ENS
received an additional award of $262,729 representing recovery of a portion of
the related legal costs which will be reflected in the first quarter of fiscal
2006.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In connection with this
matter, and in accordance with the terms of the Company's services agreement
with this customer, this customer terminated the services agreement effective October&nbsp;31,
2006.&#160;&#160; ENS may continue to provide
business services after October&nbsp;31, 2006 for this customer for electronic
transactions.&#160; Paper services for this
customer accounted for 29%, 31% and 25% of ENS&#146; total revenues in fiscal years
2005, 2004 and 2003. There is no assurance that this customer will continue any
ENS services past October&nbsp;31, 2006.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:black;font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;page-break-after:auto;text-indent:-.4in;"><b><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">13.</font></b><font size="1" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:8.5pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">Net Income Per Common Share</font></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">Basic and

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">Certain
options to purchase 105,000 and 15,000 shares of common stock, outstanding
during the year ended October&nbsp;31, 2005 and 2004, respectively, were not
included in the computation of diluted earnings per share since the exercise
price of these options was greater than the average market price of the Company&#146;s
common shares during the respective periods.&#160;
The result of their inclusion in the computation would have been
antidilutive.</font></p>

<p style="color:black;font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;page-break-after:auto;text-indent:-.4in;"><b><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">14.</font></b><font size="1" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:8.5pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">Stock Option Plans</font></p>

<p style="color:black;font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;page-break-after:auto;text-indent:-.4in;"><b><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:normal;">&nbsp;</font></b></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">The 1993
Stock Option Plan, as amended, and the 1997 Equity Incentive Plan
(collectively, the &#147;Plans&#148;) have participants which include key employees
(including officers), directors, advisors, and independent consultants to the
Company or to any of its subsidiaries.&#160;
The Company has authorized 80,000 and 300,000 shares of Common Stock for
options under the 1993 and 1997 Plans, respectively.&#160; Options granted to employees may be
designated as incentive stock options (&#147;ISO&#146;s&#148;) or non-qualified stock</font></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">options (&#147;NQSO&#146;s&#148;),
as defined by the Internal Revenue Service.&#160;
Options granted to independent consultants and other non-employees may
only be designated NQSO&#146;s.</font></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">The
exercise price of options granted under the Plans may not be less than 100% of
the fair market value of the Common Stock on the date of grant.&#160; Generally, options will be exercisable for a
term that will not exceed ten years from the date of grant.</font></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">During 2005
and 2004, the Company granted no options under the Plans.&#160; Options outstanding under the Plans have a
five year life.&#160; The vesting period is at
the discretion of the Board of Directors.&#160;&#160;
At October&nbsp;31, 2005 the Company had 50,000 options available for
grant under the Plans.</font></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">In March&nbsp;2000,
the Company adopted the 2000 Director Option Plan covering an aggregate of up
to 70,000 shares of Common Stock, pursuant to which the Company shall grant 5
year options for 5,000 shares upon the appointment of an outside director and
2,500 shares annually to each outside director on the date of the annual
stockholders meeting.&#160; Options granted
under this plan are exercisable at the fair market value of the Common Stock at
the date of the grant.&#160; In accordance
with this plan the Company granted 10,000 and 15,000 options during 2005 and
2004, respectively.&#160; These options have a
five year life.&#160; Options granted upon
appointment vest ratably over three years beginning with the grant date.&#160; Options granted annually vest immediately.</font></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

with respect to shares under option is summarized below:</font></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">The
remaining weighted average contractual life of options outstanding at October&nbsp;31,
2005 was 1.34 years.</font></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:black;font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;page-break-after:auto;text-indent:-.4in;"><b><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">15.</font></b><font size="1" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:8.5pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">Employee Benefit Plan</font></p>

<p style="color:black;font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;page-break-after:auto;text-indent:-.4in;"><b><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:normal;">&nbsp;</font></b></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">The Company
has a defined contribution plan under Section&nbsp;401(k) of the Internal
Revenue Code covering substantially all employees.&#160; The plan allows employees to make
contributions up to a specified percentage of their compensation.&#160; The Company&#146;s matching of contributions was
elective until January&nbsp;1, 2005 when the Company adopted the Safe Harbor
provisions making matching contributions mandatory. These provisions require
the Company to match all contributions (100%) made by employees up to three
percent (3%) of their compensation and half of all contributions up to the next
two percent (2%) of their compensation.&#160;
The Company contributed $117,284, $35,220 and $32,165 to the plan during
the years ended October&nbsp;31, 2005, 2004 and 2003, respectively.</font></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:black;font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;page-break-after:auto;text-indent:-.4in;"><b><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">16.</font></b><font size="1" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:8.5pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">Related-Party Transactions</font></p>

<p style="color:black;font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;page-break-after:auto;text-indent:-.4in;"><b><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:normal;">&nbsp;</font></b></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">On March&nbsp;13,
2002, the Company loaned $200,000 to an employee of ENS under a promissory note
bearing interest of 5%, due March&nbsp;13, 2007.&#160; This balance is included in other assets. The
Company also subleases office space in New York to a company owned by a former
director of the Company.&#160; The sublease,
which commenced December&nbsp;1, 1994, is on a month-to-month basis.&#160; Rental income related to this sublease was
$36,000 for the years ended October&nbsp;31, 2005, 2004 and 2003, respectively.</font></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:black;font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;page-break-after:auto;text-indent:-.4in;"><b><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">17.</font></b><font size="1" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:8.5pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">Operating Segments</font></p>

<p style="color:black;font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .4in;page-break-after:auto;text-indent:-.4in;"><b><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:normal;">&nbsp;</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company currently
operates in two operating segments:&#160; the
holding company, including certain investments which are currently not
material; and the operations of ENS.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">Segments
were determined based on products and services provided by each segment.&#160; Accounting policies of the segments are the
same as those described in the summary of significant accounting policies.&#160; The Company evaluates performance based on
profits or loss from operations before income</font></p>

<p style="color:black;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">The sum of
the quarterly net income(loss) per common share amounts do not necessarily
equal the amount for the fiscal year primarily because the earnings per share
for each quarter is computed using the weighted-average number of shares
outstanding during that quarter, while earnings per share for the fiscal year
is computed using the weighted-average number of shares outstanding during the
year.</font></p>
